title: SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective is differentiable on all of ℝᵈ and may be nonconvex. It has finite infimum f⋆ and satisfies f(x₀) − f⋆ ≤ Δ. The infimum need not be attained.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns the full vector g(x,ω) with mean ∇f(x). Calls use fresh i.i.d. seeds, including repeated calls at the same point. The public input gives d, the measurable seed space Ω, x₀, L > 0, S ≥ 0, Δ ≥ 0, and ε > 0. The objective, oracle map, sampling law, and infimum are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, Params and spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Writing σᵢ(x) = (E|gᵢ(x,ω) − ∇ᵢf(x)|²)¹ᐟ², the bound is supₓ ∑ᵢ σᵢ(x) ≤ S. The coordinate noise profile can vary with x, and coordinates within one reply may be dependent.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, spec.admissible coordinate second-moment integrability and sum-of-square-roots bound

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient satisfies ‖∇f(x) − ∇f(y)‖₁ ≤ L‖x − y‖∞ globally. The same dual ℓ₁ norm measures stationarity.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries, gradient replies, and outputs belong to ℝᵈ with public finite dimension d.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return one measurable point X with integrable ‖∇f(X)‖₁. The criterion uses the first power of the full gradient’s ℓ₁ norm.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E‖∇f(X)‖₁ ≤ ε under the product law of the algorithm seed and the oracle seed sequence, subject to the fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup pairs ℓ∞-to-ℓ₁ smoothness and expected ℓ₁ stationarity with a pointwise budget on the sum of coordinate noise standard deviations. That budget allows the noisy coordinates to change with the query point.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Stationarity with Coordinatewise Noise

We seek a stationary point of a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R in dimension d. Its gradient is Lipschitz from ℓ∞ to ℓ1, and the given starting point has bounded objective gap above the infimum. At each query, the oracle uses a fresh independent sample to return an unbiased gradient estimate with a uniform bound on the sum of its coordinate standard deviations. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈Rd satisfying E[∥∇f(x¯)∥1]≤ε, where the expectation includes both algorithm and oracle randomness.

Write f⋆ for the finite value of the optimization problem infx∈Rdf(x). The algorithm receives the dimension d∈{0,1,…}, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0∈Rd, the smoothness constant L>0, the noise bound S≥0, the initial gap bound Δ≥0, and the tolerance ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is differentiable everywhere. For every x,y∈Rd and every r∈R satisfying |xi−yi|≤r for all i=1,…,d, its gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥1≤Lr. The starting point satisfies f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Sampling and coordinatewise noise). At call k≥0 with query x∈Rd, the oracle returns g(x,ξk), where g:Rd×Ω→Rd is jointly measurable. The samples (ξk)k≥0 are independent measurable random variables with common law ν on Ω, and the entire sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. For each fixed x and ξ∼ν, the vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and each coordinate error ei(x,ξ)=gi(x,ξ)−∂if(x) is square integrable. Their moments satisfy Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),∑i=1dEξ∼ν[ei(x,ξ)2]≤S.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its gradient norm ∥∇f(x¯)∥1 must be integrable, and it must satisfy E[∥∇f(x¯)∥1]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Jeremy Bernstein, Yu-Xiang Wang, Kamyar Azizzadenesheli, and Animashree Anandkumar. signSGD: Compressed Optimisation for Non-Convex Problems. 2018. Complexity: O(B(1+Δ/(ηε))) stochastic-gradient calls for minibatch signSGD when ηLΣ/2+2SΣ/B≤ε/2, where η>0 is the step size, B≥1 is the integer batch size, LΣ=∑iLi sums the diagonal quadratic-majorant coefficients, and SΣ=∑iσi sums uniform coordinate noise standard-deviation bounds.
  • Hongyi Tao, Dingzhi Yu, and Lijun Zhang. When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on ℓ₁-norm Lower Bounds. 2026, arXiv preprint v1. Complexity: O((1+LΔ/ε2)(1+∥σ∥12/ε2)) stochastic-gradient calls for minibatch SignSGD and a uniformly sampled iterate, where σi uniformly bounds the noise standard deviation in coordinate i.
theorems.formulaHtml: (⌈8⋅L⋅Δε2⌉++1)⋅(⌈16⋅S2ε2⌉++1)

comparisonHtml:
The differentiable f:Rd→R has finite infimum, f(x0)−inff≤Δ, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥1≤L∥x−y∥∞. The jointly measurable oracle g(x,ξ) uses IID draws ξ∼p, with Epg(x,ξ)=∇f(x) and ∑isi(x)≤S at every x. For L,ε>0 and S,Δ≥0, the target is a measurable output X with E∥∇f(X)∥1≤ε.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  S : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) → ℝ
  Query q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Reply q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Output q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.S ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) → q.Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d))
      (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)) (fstar : ℝ),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, x) ω => g x ω } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y r, (∀ i, |x i - y i| ≤ r) →
        ∑ i, |gradient f x i - gradient f y i| ≤ q.L * r) ∧
      (∀ x, fstar ≤ f x) ∧ (∀ η, 0 < η → ∃ x, f x < fstar + η) ∧ f q.x0 - fstar ≤ q.Δ ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂p = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x i, Integrable (fun ω => (g x ω i - gradient f x i) ^ 2) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∑ i, Real.sqrt (∫ ω, (g x ω i - gradient f x i) ^ 2 ∂p) ≤ q.S)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ∑ i, |gradient f (output ω) i|) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ∑ i, |gradient f (output ω) i| ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth
